get.description: Unauthenticated, non-secret. The landing page's 'Open workspace' goes straight in when auth_mode is 'off'.

post.description: Use an existing installation without leaving TRACE.

get.description: Public on purpose: the browser arrives from github.com with no token. `state` is the proof of who started this.

Existing installations of TRACE's GitHub App, for when the app is already installed (GitHub then does not redirect back).
POC single-tenant behaviour: every installation of this app is listed. A multi-tenant deployment must not do this.

post.description: Halts future jobs and revokes local access immediately. Retained evidence/citations are untouched.
(Re)generate the drain signing secret. It is shown once: paste it into Vercel's Drain 'signature secret' together with the URL.

get.description: Discovery with credentials kept server-side. GitHub: repositories. Vercel: projects. Bounded (5 pages).

post.description: The replacement is verified *before* activation; if it fails the working credential stays in force.
Public on purpose: the application posts here. The HMAC-SHA256 signature is the authentication; the answer acknowledges durable receipt.
Public on purpose: Vercel posts here. The HMAC signature is the authentication. The response acknowledges durable receipt, not analysis.

Creates the project, adopts the draft's connections, applies log scope and repository selections (re-validated
against provider discovery). Skipped/unverified stages stay visibly unfinished; nothing is faked as ready.
`index_job_ids` is empty until code indexing (T-007) exists - repositories are bound, not yet indexed.

get.description:
Only projects the caller holds a grant on. 'No projects' and 'no matches' are distinguishable via
meta.coverage.total_authorized (empty dataset vs. empty search).

delete.description:
Permanently delete a project and everything TRACE holds for it: its evidence graph, stored logs and deployments,
connections and their sealed credentials, repository bindings, jobs and members. The audit trail is kept.
The graph is cleared first, so a graph failure leaves the project intact instead of leaving orphaned evidence.

parameters.description: Also delete tickets assigned to this project; otherwise they return to 'Need a project'

put.description:
Upsert by key; environments absent from the list are removed only if nothing references them yet.
Existing IDs are stable across renames so historical manifests are never invalidated.

get.description: Evidence viewer: log events and source chunks by id, scoped to the project.
Published code graph (symbols and structural relationships). Structure only: static reachability is never runtime proof.

`trace`: the project's backbone (scope, sources, revisions, deployments, tickets, investigations, findings) plus recent
error events. `label`: the newest nodes of one label. `type`: up to 100 relationships of one type with their endpoints.
Relationships among the returned nodes are always included.
Latest run per repository binding, newest first. The UI polls this while a run is queued or running.

post.description:
Queue indexing of the project's bound repositories at their selected branch/commit. Read-only against GitHub.
A repository that already has a queued or running request returns that request instead of starting another.

get.description: One node with all its properties and its relationship counts by type, direction and neighbour label.
Expand a node (double-click in Neo4j Browser): its neighbours, optionally of one relationship type and direction.
Trace: the shortest chain of relationships between two nodes (any type, either direction), inside the project.

Labels and relationship types present in this project's graph, with counts (Neo4j Browser's database overview), plus the
ontology they come from and how many stored events have not reached the graph yet.
Find nodes by name, title, path, message, commit or id.
One symbol with its callers, callees and the exact pinned source chunks (content hash included).

post.description:
Load the project's deployments, PulseLab ticket evidence and ingested log evidence from the control plane into the evidence graph
(idempotent). Ingested logs are normally applied by the worker as they arrive; this applies whatever is due now (bounded) and reports what
the graph has acknowledged. `retry_failed=true` re-queues rows the graph refused earlier.
Create (or reconfigure) the project's app-log source and generate its signing secret, shown once. Calling again rotates the secret.

get.description: Stored logs only (filters are TRACE filters, not provider query syntax). 'Nothing stored' and 'nothing matched' are told apart.

post.description: Explicit 'Fetch from source': a bounded, read-only live capture. It stores what arrives during the window; it is not history.

get.description: Per-resource freshness. 'No events yet' is a gap, never healthy; 'available' means events were actually received.
Any project reader sees the team; org admins see it too for administration.

put.description:
Replaces the grant list. Guards: every user must be an active org member; environment ids must belong to
the project; at least one admin must remain so the project is never orphaned.
One repo can map to many services and a service to many repos/paths; never inferred from names.

get.description: Latest schema snapshot of the project's database. `connected:false` / `captured:false` say what is missing; no tables are invented.

Structure as CONFIGURED in TRACE plus deployment facts from the provider. Nothing here is 'observed in logs': every edge
carries its origin so the UI can label it. Unknown links are listed as gaps instead of being drawn.

Server-side search/filter/sort with bounded pages. meta.coverage.counts has the per-view totals (within the
current scope filters) so the UI can show 'Need a project 2' without a second request.

post.description: Manual form and authenticated API. Re-sending the same external_id is idempotent (unchanged / new revision).
Explicit Investigate / Rerun. Assigning or opening a ticket never calls this.

get.description: The redacted original export (requests, backend events, gaps) for the ticket detail 'raw evidence' view.
